U. S. DEPARTMENT of
AGRICULTURE, and
PULASKI COUNTY cooperating
Court House - Winamac, Indiana 46996 - Phone 946-3412
April 25, 1972
Prosecuting Attorney
Pulaski County
III N. Monticello
Winamac, Indiana 46996
Dear Mr. Tankersley,
I believe that there are several advantages to your proposed marijuana control program in relation to environmental protection.
The most important, I feel, is the use of a granular material which is much easier to control in application. The same dosage rate is to be used as would be for a liquid spray. The use of granulars eliminates the danger of spray mist settling into the drainage ditches or damaging crops. Granted that some granulars may fall into the water, at least the potential for preventing any large introduction into the ditch is much greater with the granular material.
Secondly, I believe the control program by one agency far outweighs large indiscriminate individual herbicide applications. Mr. Clark has discussed this project with Purdue Agronomist, Weed Control Specialist, and the Indiana Steam Pollution Control Staff. His primary interest has been environment protection coupled with good control methods. Law enforcement agencies, Cooperative Extension Service, Soil and Water Conservation Service, and the State Wildlife Conservation Service all working with one control applicator has outstanding merit in the consideration of the environment.
One other advantage of this program will be its demonstration value to help illustrate to the land owners how to control marijuana in a practical manner. Therefore, it will encourage individual interest in participating in the control program. Protection of our young people should also be one of our prime concerns in environment protection.
Sincerely,
Jack M. Hart
Area Extension Agent
Jack m. Wart
